description: β numerical validation — Monte Carlo check of the analytical variance formula for the octonion associator, Fano-triple case. Setup (per docs/research/variance_of_associator.md § "Worked example:
comments: β numerical validation — Monte Carlo check of the analytical variance
formula for the octonion associator, Fano-triple case.
Setup (per docs/research/variance_of_associator.md § "Worked example:
single Fano generator"):
A(a, b, c) := ‖[a, b, c]‖²   where [a,b,c] = (a·b)·c − a·(b·c)
Unperturbed: [a,b,c] = 2·e_7, A = 4.
Perturb a_1 → 1 + δ, δ ~ N(0, σ²). The analytical first-order GUM
variance (from the β document, derivation):
Var(A) ≈ 64 σ²                                (TRUTH)
If the current compiler's stepwise scalar-product rule were applied
instead, it would give:
Var_compiler(A) ≈ 16 σ²                       (COMPILER, 4× low)
This test computes the sample variance of A over N = 100,000 Monte
Carlo samples and compares to the TRUTH formula. It does NOT test the
compiler's variance_of() — that requires the full Knowledge<f64>
chain which introduces unrelated complexities (see ζ buffer bug). The
compiler comparison is deferred to a separate test.
Pass criterion: |MC_var − 64σ²| / 64σ² < 0.05 (5% relative error).
If this passes, β's analytical formula is validated empirically. The
remaining claim — that the compiler produces 16σ² — is then a
separate reading-confirmation task.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `tuple_return_sret_r12_slot`. A tuple-returning function that CALLS another tuple-returning function used to destroy its caller's aggregate-return pointer. The x86 SRET prologue is `push rbp; mov rbp,rsp; push r12; sub rsp,frame`, so. It should compile and run successfully. Expected stdout: TUPLE_SRET_R12_OK
description: A tuple-returning function that CALLS another tuple-returning function used to destroy its caller's aggregate-return pointer. The x86 SRET prologue is `push rbp; mov rbp,rsp; push r12; sub rsp,frame`, so
comments: A tuple-returning function that CALLS another tuple-returning function used to
destroy its caller's aggregate-return pointer.
The x86 SRET prologue is `push rbp; mov rbp,rsp; push r12; sub rsp,frame`, so
the saved r12 lives at rbp-0x08 -- which was also slot 1, where the incoming
SRET pointer was stored. `pop r12` then restored that pointer instead of the
caller's r12, and the caller wrote its result through a pointer into the
callee's dead frame. The next call reused those bytes, so every binding read
the LAST call's values.
Confirmed under gdb: r12 intact at the callee's entry, holding the callee's
own SRET at its `ret`. Fixed by reserving slot 1 for the pushed r12.
Two bindings minimum: with one, a stale pointer still reads its own values.

instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `u64_const_fold_witness`. Finding 11 (issue #2084): const_prop folds u64 >>, /, % with unsigned semantics — without this, fold_binop_int would treat operands as i64 and produce the wrong magnitudes at bit 63. It should compile and run successfully.
description: Finding 11 (issue #2084): const_prop folds u64 >>, /, % with unsigned semantics — without this, fold_binop_int would treat operands as i64 and produce the wrong magnitudes at bit 63.
comments: Finding 11 (issue #2084): const_prop folds u64 >>, /, % with unsigned
semantics — without this, fold_binop_int would treat operands as i64
and produce the wrong magnitudes at bit 63.
Witnesses 4 cases that all hit the literal-only fold path (no binary
IR ever gets emitted for these expressions; they compile to IrLoadImm
via const_prop ->  cp_u64_div / cp_u64_mod / cp_u64_shr):
0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF_u64 /  2   == 0x7FFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF   (cp_u64_div)
0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF_u64 >> 4   == 0x0FFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF  (cp_u64_shr)
0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF_u64 >> 64  == 0                      (cp_u64_shr, n>=64)
The equality comparisons then anchor the folded values at runtime.
Under the signed fold path these would each be a different number:
0xFFFF.. / 2  = 0          in i64 truncate-toward-zero
0xFFFF.. % 3  = -1         in i64 truncate-toward-zero
0xFFFF.. >> 4 = 0xFFFFFFFF in i64 arithmetic shift
0xFFFF.. >> 64 = (out of range, BOTTOM -> no fold)
and each assert below would catch that signed result.
